# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 12 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_012_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 12

**12:1** And she finished the purple and the scarlet and brought them to the priest. The priest blessed her, saying: "Mary, the Lord God has magnified your name, and you shall be blessed among all the generations of the earth."

**12:2** And Mary rejoiced and went to visit her kinswoman Elizabeth. She knocked at the door. When Elizabeth heard it, she set down the scarlet thread and ran to the door and opened it. Seeing Mary, she blessed her and said: "How has this come to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For behold, what is in me leaped and blessed you."

**12:3** And Mary forgot the mysteries which the angel Gabriel had told her, and she looked up toward heaven and said: "Who am I, Lord, that all the generations of the earth shall call me blessed?"

**12:4** And she remained three months with Elizabeth. Day by day her womb grew, and Mary was afraid and went to her house and hid herself from the children of Israel. And she was sixteen years old when these mysteries happened to her.

---

## Translator's Note

Mary's age is given as sixteen at 12:4 — the text is insistent throughout about her youth, partly as a purity credential and partly as dramatic contrast with Joseph's declared old age in ch. 9. The extraordinary note in 12:3 — "Mary forgot the mysteries which the angel Gabriel had told her" — is psychologically vivid and has no parallel in canonical Gospels. Elizabeth's greeting closely follows Luke 1:43-44 but adds "and blessed you," attributing the quickening to Mary's blessing rather than to the hearing of her voice alone.
